major_concerns: Hosted-LLM nondeterminism and single-model dependence threaten exact reproducibility and may inflate apparent GVR gains.
Deterministic verifiers (syntax, reachability, ACL) may miss high-level semantic/policy violations leading to false assurance.
Simulated vendor templates/topologies in Mininet may not capture device-specific quirks of real multi-vendor hardware, risking overgeneralization.
Preregistration lacks explicit power/sample-size justification for McNemar/Wilcoxon tests and failure-mode subgroup analyses.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact LLM model identifier(s), temperature/seed policies, and retry rules; predefine procedures for repeated runs to quantify variance.
Extend verifier coverage or add adjudication for semantic/policy checks (e.g., policy-rule formalization or human oracle for ambiguous cases).
Add stratified vendor-template selection and include at least one hardware-proximate variability test or explain limitations explicitly.
Provide sample-size/power calculation for paired comparisons and predefine handling of nondeterministic API failures and retries.

major_concerns: Operational 'harm' labels depend strongly on emulation fidelity and predefined harmful outcomes—risk of label mismatch to real-world harms.
Multi-sample approaches increase model-call cost/latency; operational tradeoffs (human-review load reduction vs cost) need explicit quantification.
Semantic-entropy and agreement metrics require precise definition and calibration; thresholds chosen on validation fold may not generalize.
Risk of false negatives on rare but severe semantic errors not well addressed.
required_design_repairs: Define harm taxonomy and emulation instrumentation in detail; justify that chosen emulation outcomes map to operationally consequential harms.
Provide explicit semantic-entropy computation formula, tokenization details, and multi-sample generation procedure (sampling seeds/temperature).
Include cost/latency analysis showing detector deployment feasibility at target false-positive rates and an a priori power analysis for AUC estimation.
Add robustness checks: alternate thresholds, cross-validation, and sensitivity analysis to emulation assumptions; plan for human-oracle adjudication of ambiguous cases.

major_concerns: Reliance on deterministic verifiers/emulation for labeling may under-detect subtle semantic faults or misclassify borderline cases.
Using a single hosted LLM model limits generality of the catalog; prompt-engineering choices may dominate observed distributions.
Public-task sampling may underrepresent rare but critical production intents; representativeness unclear.
Retry-policy definitions insufficiently precise (e.g., what constitutes 'syntax-only' repair).
required_design_repairs: Adopt adjudication protocol (automated+human spot checks) to validate verifier labels and estimate label error-rate.
Clarify and preregister exact prompt templates, retry-policy algorithms, and selection criteria for intents; include stratified sampling to cover rare-critical categories.
Consider multi-model replication (at least one other model) or sensitivity checks to show catalog stability across models.
Report latency/cost tradeoffs per retry policy and include an analysis of operational acceptability for increased latency.

major_concerns: Perfect bytewise reproducibility is unlikely when using hosted LLMs; the protocol must distinguish reproducible verifier outputs from nonreproducible LLM artifacts.
External dependencies and package/version drift can compromise reproducibility unless pinned and archived.
Publication of configuration artifacts risks leaking sensitive/proprietary data unless sanitization is strictly defined.
required_design_repairs: Pin and archive all software dependencies (container images, package wheels) and record cryptographic hashes; include an instructionized reproducibility checklist.
Provide a deterministic LLM-stub mode or offline model snapshot for exact-replay experiments, or clearly document expected nondeterminism and metrics to quantify it.
Define and implement an explicit sanitization policy for published artifacts; include legal/ethics checklist for artifact sharing.
Predefine acceptance criterion for 'reproducible' (e.g., verifier-output equivalence vs. full artifact hash match) and add root-cause classification procedures for mismatches.
